newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian money market rates steady, demand weaker.
newsitem.headline: Croatian money market rates steady, demand weaker.

text.p: Croatia's money market rates held steady on Wednedsay despite weaker demand by banks, which also borrowed from the central bank, dealers said.
"For the first time in days we have seen higher supply of kuna and there was money left after the demand was met in full," a dealer told Reuters.

Trade totalled 21.3 million kuna by 0900 GMT, leaving some 26 million on offer. Banks took out another 117 million kuna in five-day repurchase funds from the National Bank of Croatia after repaying a previous borrowing.
Most of the money market deals were call money loans at an unchanged 10.5 percent.
One-week deals were struck at 10 and 11 percent, while one-month borrowings were made at 15 and 16 percent, the latter rate paid by a savings bank.

Tuesday's overnight trade totalled 96.4 million kuna, sought by one bank to cover its shortfall and several others to maintain their mandatory reserves. -- Sandra Kalogjera, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
